(See page IV-40, Scope of Statements.)" and "(20) If, at the time of execution of an UNSTRING statement, the conditions described in general rule 17 are not encountered, ..."; the box closes only after "UNSTRING statement." at the end of rule (20).
claim.markdown_says:
(19) The END-UNSTRING phrase delimits the scope of the UNSTRING statement. (See page IV-40, Scope of Statements.)

(20) If, at the time of execution of an UNSTRING statement, the conditions described in general rule 17 are not encountered, ...
claim.why_it_matters: The box marks level-2 (high level) specifications. Rules (19) and (20) carry no box markers, so the END-UNSTRING and NOT ON OVERFLOW rules read as level 1, while rules (14)-(18) beside them on the same page keep their markers.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 371 (VI-139) shows one continuous rectangle from above rule (14) down to below the final line 'UNSTRING statement.' of rule (20); its left and right edges run unbroken past rules (19) and (20), and the bottom edge sits under rule (20). In page-371.md, rules (14) through (18), including 17a and 17b, are wrapped in the ║ level-2 markers, but rules (19) and (20) have none. The text of both rules is present and matches. Only the level marking is lost, and that marking is normative because it tells which level the END-UNSTRING scope rule and the NOT ON OVERFLOW rule belong to. The claim describes this accurately.
